title: Agent-side failures are reclassified as infrastructure failures in pairing coverage
claim: When an Agent process crashes, times out, or emits a rejected stream, the assembled runner records the sealed trial's pairing fact as TrialOutcome::InfrastructureFailure, so pair coverage labels the trial 'infrastructure-failure:<id>' and removes it from the Agent outcome class. The comparison vocabulary has no Agent-failure outcome at all. This contradicts the mandatory clause that Agent crashes and Agent-owned timeouts on valid tasks remain Agent outcomes and are never reclassified as infrastructure.

evidence.detail: let outcome = if agent_failed { TrialOutcome::InfrastructureFailure } else if verifier_failed { TrialOutcome::GraderFailure } else { TrialOutcome::ValidAgentOutcome }; - agent_failed covers every AgentCompletion::Failed including non-zero exit, timeout, and cancellation.
enum TrialOutcome { ValidAgentOutcome, InfrastructureFailure, GraderFailure } - no Agent-outcome failure variant exists, so an Agent failure cannot remain an Agent outcome in coverage.
p18_a05 asserts pairs[0]['comparability'].starts_with('infrastructure-failure:') for adapter/evidence stream failures.

p18_a06 asserts the same 'infrastructure-failure:' comparability for agent-timeout and agent-cancelled, whose receipts carry boundary 'agent-process' - an Agent-owned timeout presented as infrastructure.

'An Agent failure remains scored under the native grader and is never reclassified as infrastructure merely to protect a result.' and P18-FAL-003 'Agent crashes and Agent-owned timeouts on valid tasks MUST remain Agent outcomes'.
Exit-blocking threshold: 'one valid Agent failure reclassified to protect the result'.

reproduction: cargo test -p opi-eval --test phase18_assembled_smoke p18_a06_process_timeout_cancellation_race (green; asserts the infrastructure-failure label for an agent-process-boundary timeout)
inspect crates/opi-eval/src/runner/experiment.rs run_trial fact construction and crates/opi-eval/src/comparison.rs TrialOutcome

title: Verifier-native artifacts are staged under the agent-product source identity
claim: run_trial stages the verifier's stdout, stderr, and native report into the sealed bundle with SourceIdentity 'agent-<product>' (one source variable reused for agent and verifier staging), so grader-produced bytes carry an agent-source attribution in the sealed manifest. The report path works around this by matching grader artifacts on role suffix. The ledger flagged this for 18.15 cleanup; it remains unresolved at audit_head.

evidence.detail: let source = SourceIdentity::new(&format!("agent-{product}")) ...; the same source stages native/verifier-stdout.log, native/verifier-stderr.log, and the verifier's native report.
headline() identifies the admitted native grader report by key suffix (ctrf-report/pier-report) plus Native role rather than by a grader source identity.
'bundle manifests label the verifier's native report source agent-<product> ... source-identity cleanup flagged for 18.15' - not applied; 18.15 flags do not record the fix.

reproduction: grep -n 'SourceIdentity::new(&format!("agent-' crates/opi-eval/src/runner/experiment.rs and inspect the verifier staging calls that reuse it

title: DeepSWE oracle preflight bar is structural verification, not a reward-positive check
claim: run_oracle_preflight accepts any Verified DeepSWE completion as a passing oracle preflight (adapter_key 'deepswe-v1.1' => true), without requiring the reference solution's rewards to be positive. A zero-reward reference solution - the signature of a broken or mis-collected task - would pass the preflight and the task would be admitted. The pier aggregate exposes readable per-metric rewards (the real preflight earned 1.0), so a positive-reward bar was implementable. Terminal-Bench keeps a positive passed counter; only DeepSWE is weakened.

evidence.detail: let passing = match &record.completion { BenchmarkCompletion::Verified { .. } => match inputs.adapter_key.as_str() { "deepswe-v1.1" => true, _ => matches!(&metrics.passed, Some(Fact::Known { value, .. }) if *value > 0) }, _ => false };
import_pier_job_result parses and validates per-metric rewards (integral, finite) but the preflight never requires them positive.

reproduction: cargo test -p opi-eval --lib runner (unit suites cover import_pier_job_result shapes but no zero-reward oracle rejection exists)

title: Native conformance-rerun receipt hardcodes cases_run=12 while the stage runs 13 cases
claim: scripts/phase18-native-smoke.sh cmd_conformance_rerun iterates 13 case specs (2 opi agent, 2 pi agent, 3 tb21, 3 tb30, 3 deepswe) but writes a receipt with cases_run=12. The sealed artifact's conformance receipt therefore misreports the executed case count. The 18.15 review flagged it for 18.16 absorption; it is unresolved at audit_head.

evidence.detail: the for-case list contains 13 entries: agent opi completed/identity, agent pi completed/identity, terminal-bench-2.1 completed/identity/immutable-capture, terminal-bench-3.0 completed/identity/immutable-capture, deepswe completed/identity/immutable-capture.
'the conformance receipt still records cases_run 12 for 13 actual cases (18.16 absorbs it)' - 18.16 session notes record no such change.

reproduction: sed -n '1154,1215p' scripts/phase18-native-smoke.sh and count the case list vs the receipt constant
